slides.title: ‘Product’
slides.text:
‘Product’
A product is anything that can be offered to a market to satisfy a want or need.
Product can be tangible (goods) or intangible (services, ideas)

bullets.text: A product is anything that can be offered to a market to satisfy a want or need.
Product can be tangible (goods) or intangible (services, ideas)

slides.title: Types of Consumer Products
slides.text:
Types of Consumer Products
Convenience Products
Day to day use
Frequently bought
Minimal comparison and effort
Readily available
Shopping Products
Relatively less frequently purchased
Comparison on price, quality, styles
Time and effort in gathering information
Speciality Products
Special purchase effort because of uniqueness and brand identification
Less comparison of brands
Unsought Products
Low product awareness

slides.title: Generic Product:
slides.text:
Generic Product:
Basic features of a product
Essential attributes to deliver the core benefit to the customers.
A place to sit, order, eat food: Tables, Chairs, Menu

bullets.text: Essential attributes to deliver the core benefit to the customers.

slides.title: Expected Level/ Product
slides.text:
Expected Level/ Product
A set of attributes that a customer expects when purchasing a product
Generic product + the minimum that a customer expects from a product in the category.
Includes features, design, style, quality
Quality food, hygienic ambience, friendly staff

bullets.text: A set of attributes that a customer expects when purchasing a product

Quality food, hygienic ambience, friendly staff

slides.title: Augmented Product
slides.text:
Augmented Product
Additional services, features, benefits, experiences that go beyond customer expectations
Unexpected value enhancing elements
Examples: Warranties, instruction manual, repair services, toll-free services
Restaurant example: Complimentary appetizer, live music, personalized greetings, meal suggestions, valet parking

slides.text:
Potential Product
Future possibilities for a product
Potential improvements for a product to beat the competition
Example: AI powered menu, Virtual reality dining experience, Plant based menu, Dietary preferences, Theme dinners

slides.title: Bases of Product Differentiation

Bases of Product Differentiation
Core functionality: Primary benefit
Features: Supplement basic function
Performance quality: Level at which the product’s primary characteristics operate.

bullets.text: Performance quality: Level at which the product’s primary characteristics operate.

slides.text:
Conformance quality: the degree to which all the produced units are identical and meet the promised specifications.
Durability: Expected operating life under natural or stressful conditions.
Reliability: Product’s intended performance over a specific period of time.
